newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson's TMM mulls two German factory closures.
newsitem.headline: Thomson's TMM mulls two German factory closures.

text.p: Thomson Multimedia, the consumer electronics branch of the French state-owned Thomson group, said it was studying cutbacks in its television manufacturing operations in Germany that could affect 800 jobs.
"The company is confronted with heavy cost handicaps compared to its competitors," Thomson Television Germany, a TMM subsidiary, said in a statement.

"Thomson Multimedia will be forced to consider production shutdowns which could affect the 800 jobs existing today in its Celle and Hannover plants, approximately one third of its total personnel in Germany," it said.

After a bungled effort last year to privatise Thomson in one piece, the French government has decided to sell the defence electronics business Thomson-CSF first and then sell TMM after injecting billions of francs into the money-losing company.
Thomson Television Germany said its supervisory board would meet at the end of the month to review the situation of the TV manufacturing activities in Celle and Hannover.

"The persistent fall in industry volume sales, coupled with significant price erosion on consumer electronics markets and attendant profitability issues mean that Thomson Multimedia must reorganise manufacturing activities in Europe," it said.
